learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback appears. Entry checks are low stakes, and a missed fresh re-entry returns control without exit credit.

items.title: Starting check: compare pH with pI
items.prompt: Protein A has pI 6.0 and is placed in buffer at pH 8.0. What is its approximate net charge?
options: Net positive because pH is above pI
Net negative because pH is above pI
Exactly neutral because every protein is neutral at pH 8
Permanently positive regardless of buffer pH
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: predict electrode direction
items.prompt: A native protein has pI 9.0 in a pH 7.0 buffer. The left electrode is negative and the right electrode is positive. Which direction is expected?
options: Toward the positive right electrode because the protein is negative
No movement because every native protein is neutral
Toward the negative left electrode as a positive protein
Toward both electrodes at the same time
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: identify an isoelectric focus
items.prompt: A protein migrates through a stable pH gradient and stops where local pH equals 5.2. What does 5.2 most directly represent?
options: The protein’s isoelectric point
The protein’s molecular mass in kilodaltons
The SDS concentration in the gel
The voltage of the negative electrode
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: rank SDS-PAGE migration
items.prompt: Two single-chain proteins are fully denatured with SDS. Protein X is 30 kDa and Protein Y is 90 kDa. Which result is expected?
options: Y moves farther because it contains more amino acids
Both stop at their pI values in the SDS gel
Both move identically because SDS removes all size effects
X moves farther because its chain is smaller
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: integrate charge and electrode labels
items.prompt: Protein M has pI 8.4 in a pH 5.4 native buffer. The cathode is labelled negative. What behavior is most likely?
options: M is negative and migrates away from the cathode
M is positive and migrates toward the cathode
M is neutral and focuses at every point in the buffer
M receives a uniform negative SDS coat
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: compare focusing positions
items.prompt: An isoelectric-focusing gradient runs from pH 4 on the left to pH 10 on the right. Protein R has pI 5 and Protein S has pI 9. Which pattern is expected?
options: R and S both focus at pH 7 because size controls focusing
R focuses near pH 9 and S near pH 5
R focuses left of S at their respective pI values
SDS drives both proteins to the far-right edge
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: rebuild the charge-sign rule
items.prompt: Which rule correctly predicts protein net charge?
options: Below pI is positive; above pI is negative
pH below pI gives net negative; pH above pI gives net positive
Every protein is neutral whenever pH is not 7
Protein charge depends only on molecular mass
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: apply the sign rule again
items.prompt: Protein Q has pI 4.5 in a pH 7.5 native buffer. Which electrode attracts Q?
options: The negative electrode because Q is positive
Neither electrode because Q is exactly neutral
Both electrodes because Q has two charges
The positive electrode because Q is negative
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: compare focusing positions
items.prompt: In an isoelectric-focusing gradient that increases in pH from left to right, which rule correctly compares two proteins’ positions?
options: Lower pI focuses farther left; higher pI focuses farther right
Lower mass focuses farther left; higher mass focuses farther right
More negative charge always focuses left; positive charge always focuses right
Greater SDS binding focuses left; weaker SDS binding focuses right
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: compare new focusing positions
items.prompt: A fresh isoelectric-focusing gradient runs from pH 3 on the left to pH 11 on the right. Protein U has pI 6.2 and Protein V has pI 8.7. Which pattern is expected?
options: U and V both focus near pH 7 because size fixes position
U focuses near pH 8.7 while V focuses near pH 6.2
U focuses near pH 6.2 left of V, which focuses near pH 8.7
V reaches the far-right edge because larger pI prevents focusing
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Starting check: infer binding from complementarity
items.prompt: A protein pocket is negatively charged at the decisive contact. Which ligand feature most directly supports selective binding there?
options: A second negative group aimed at the contact
A bulky group that cannot enter the pocket
A neutral surface located far from the pocket
A positive group positioned at the contact
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: predict a pocket mutation
items.prompt: A mutation removes a hydrophobic side chain that forms the wall of a ligand pocket, but the protein remains folded. What is the most direct prediction?
options: The protein must become a DNA molecule
Affinity may fall after pocket complementarity changes
Every immune cell in the body stops functioning
The ligand becomes covalently attached more strongly
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: identify antibody recognition
items.prompt: Which feature most directly determines whether an antibody binds a supplied antigen epitope?
options: The total number of cells in the organism
The color used to draw the antigen
Shape and chemistry match at the binding site
The molecular mass of every unrelated protein
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: predict denaturation effect
items.prompt: A carrier protein is denatured so its ligand-binding pocket collapses. Which outcome is most likely?
options: Selective ligand binding decreases
The protein gains a perfectly matched pocket
The ligand becomes part of the protein sequence
All proteins acquire the same conformation
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: analyze an antibody interface
items.prompt: An antibody pocket has a positive rim that contacts a negative epitope group. A mutation changes the rim to negative while preserving overall folding. What is expected?
options: Binding strengthens because like charges attract
The antibody becomes a motor protein
The epitope is converted into an enzyme
Binding weakens after the charge reversal
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: interpret a motor cycle
items.prompt: A motor diagram shows track binding, a nucleotide-linked conformational shift, forward movement, and release. A mutation prevents the conformational shift but not initial binding. What is most likely?
options: The motor moves faster because the step is skipped
Static binding remains, but forward stepping falls
The track is converted into a ligand pocket
Every antibody loses antigen recognition
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: rebuild the interface test
items.prompt: Which comparison best predicts selective protein binding?
options: Whole-protein color and drawing size
Pocket–partner shape and contact chemistry
Organism age and unrelated cell count
The alphabetical order of protein names
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: analyze a new binding pocket
items.prompt: A receptor pocket contains a hydrogen-bond donor aimed at a ligand acceptor. A mutation removes the donor but leaves pocket shape intact. What is expected?
options: Affinity may fall because one favorable contact is lost
Affinity must rise because fewer contacts always bind better
The ligand becomes a covalent part of the receptor
The receptor becomes an antibody class
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: identify the motor-function sequence
items.prompt: Which sequence best describes a bounded motor-protein cycle?
options: Permanent binding → no conformational change → no release
Antigen binding → antibody synthesis → DNA replication
Track binding → conformational change → step → release
Protein denaturation → random diffusion → permanent attachment
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: predict another motor defect
items.prompt: A motor can undergo its conformational shift but cannot release its rear track contact. What outcome is most likely?
options: The motor becomes an antibody
The motor crosses the membrane as a hormone
The motor catalyzes glycogen synthesis
Cycling fails because attachment cannot reset
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.
